newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - May 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - May 29.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Canberra Cannons owner Col Alexander has criticised the National Basketball League for failing to cite Townsville Suns guard Simon Kerle for an alleged elbowing incident. The incident forced Cannons centre Simon Dwight from the court but NBL chief executve Bill Palmer found Kerle had no charge to answer. However Palmer did describe Kerle's defensive technique as dangerous, and said he would be cited if he did it again. Page 20.

New South Wales won last night's Australian Rugby League State of Origin game against Queensland 8-6, after leading 8-0 at half-time. The first game in the best of three series was played at Suncorp Stadium in front of a crowd of 28,222. Page 22.

Australian cricket team manager Alan Crompton has issued a statement clarifying the role of selectors, following intense speculation about the future of captain Mark Taylor. Crompton said the appointed tour selectors were captain Mark Taylor, vice-captain Steve Waugh and coach Geoff Marsh, and they did not have to consult with the Australian Cricket Board or the national selectors on their decision. Page 22.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

A report launched by Federal Sports Minister Warwick Smith yesterday warned that some elite female athletes were adopting a "sex sells" approach to gain media coverage of women's sport. The report found that coverage of women's sport was still pitifully low. Page 52.

Sydney Turf Club stewards criticised apprentice jockey Carolyn Mason for "lack of initiative" after she finished fifth on Bold Amy in the Greenacre Handicap yesterday. Mason admitted to stewards she rode Bold Amy "without judgment". Page 53.

Former Australian cricket captain Ian Chappell said yesterday current captain Mark Taylor should be dropped from the Australian test team. Speaking on Channel Nine's Today programme, Chappell questioned whether Taylor's poor form was a prolonged slump or whther he was "gone". Page 54.
THE AGE

Carlton midfielder Greg Williams, suspended by the Australian Football League Tribunal for nine matches for interfering with an umpire in round one, may retire early rather than play out the end of his last season if a ruling by the Supreme Court does notoverturn the penalty. Justice John Hedigan will hand down his decision this morning. Page B8.

The Australian Football League's national umpiring director Bill Deller is believed to have been reprimanded by senior League officials after he described last weekend's umpiring as the worst this year. AFL chief executive Wayne Jackson admitted it was posible umpires were not performing at their maximum potential, but regarded Deller's comments as unhelpful. Page B8.

The Australian Football League and its clubs are lobbying the Melbourne Cricket Club to lower the cost of opening the Melbourne Cricket Ground on Sundays, claiming the higher cost of paying staff penalty rates results in thousands of dollars of lost revenue. The break-even attendance for Sunday games is 30,000 compared to 21,000 to 24,000 on Saturdays. Page B6.
THE HERALD SUN

St Kilda ruckman Lazar Vidovic was fined at least A$750 last night by the Australian Football League Tribunal for shaking the goalpost while the ball was in transit during last Friday's reserves game against Richmond. Vidovic pleaded guilty to an uncharaceristically light-hearted Tribunal, but said he did not know his prank was a reportable offence. Page 86.

Australian tennis player Mark Woodforde beat Spaniard Javier Sanchez 5-7 7-6 (8-6) 6-7 (10-12) 6-4 8-6 in a four hour, 15 minute first round match at the French Open yesterday. Other Australians to win their first round matches were: Mark Philippoussis, Json Stoltenberg, Sandon Stolle, Todd Woodbridge and Patrick Rafter. Page 81.

Richmond forward Matthew Richardson wants to make a comeback in Saturday's Australian Football League match against Melbourne, less than a month after suffering a broken left forearm and dislocated elbow. Club doctor Chris Bradshaw cleared Richardson to pay this weekend, two weeks earlier than expected. Page 88.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

The Australian hockey team were defeated by Pakistan 3-2 at the State Hockey Centre yesterday, levelling the series at two all with two games left to play. The Australian Kookaburras scored after just 25 seconds, but Pakistan replied to lead 2-1 at half-tme. Page 85.

The Australian Capital Territory Rugby Union has put its recruitment and contracting on hold to allow the ACT Brumbies to concentrate on preparations for Saturday's Super 12 grand final against Auckland. ACTRU general manager Mark Sinderberry said he was confident of signing up all the outstanding players after Saturday's final. Page 81.

Former champions Randwick are at the bottom of the league ladder after being defeated by Bankstown 56-48 in round six of the Dairy Farmers State Netball League in Sydney last night. Randwick are yet to win a game this season. Page 87.
